candidates.title: Directed anchor-to-codeword margin with pair-separation barrier
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the swapped-source/target loss is unchanged, any declared nonzero gradient is zero or non-finite, or the exported codes fail any measured requirement: level-0 Gini exceeds control, L1-to-L2 branches per code fall below control, train-to-test frequency drift grows, sequence information falls, or pair-level ER does not rise.
candidates.risk: The source-anchored margin may improve local assignment margins without preserving useful sequence information, prefix branching, or train-to-test frequency stability. The separation barrier protects only observed selected pairs and may leave harmful codebook movements elsewhere; the frozen downstream evaluation may consequently show no gain even if the export changes and ER rises.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The assignment-margin term moves the source-selected codeword relative to the source's nearest alternative; the separation barrier acts only when the selected source and target codewords are closer than s, pushing those two codewords apart. Its gradient is zero once their squared separation reaches s. It therefore cannot pull a transition's two codewords together. Nearest-codeword indices are stop-gradient, avoiding unstable gradients through argmin.

candidates.title: Directed assignment-mass and prefix-branch balancing
candidates.falsifier: The immediate falsifier is a checker measurement of zero codebook gradient, which confirms it cannot be an admitted training candidate under the host constraint. Also falsified as a useful structural signal if swapping source and target leaves its loss unchanged on the checker batch.
candidates.risk: This term is a measurement of assignment structure rather than a trainable mechanism under the given interface: hard indicators have zero derivatives. It may satisfy the directedness check because swapping source and target changes the directed transition counts, but it cannot move the codebook or improve exported codes. It should be rejected at the gradient probe and incur no cold run.
candidates.codebook_interaction: This is a discrete assignment-structure objective. With hard argmin assignments and stop-gradient indices, its gradient with respect to codebook entries is exactly zero; it changes no codewords during training and cannot pull transition codewords together. It is not admissible under the stated requirement that a surviving candidate reach the codebook and alter export, so it is included only as a structurally distinct probe and should be rejected before a cold run unless the checker accepts zero codebook gradient.

candidates.title: Behaviour-conditioned residual alignment with endpoint repulsion
candidates.falsifier: Reject if source-target exchange does not change the loss, any declared gradient is zero or non-finite, or the resulting export fails any measured requirement: level-0 Gini no greater than control, L1-to-L2 branches per code at least control, train-to-test frequency drift no greater than control, sequence information no lower than control, and pair-level ER increased.
candidates.risk: Residual-direction alignment may encode a generic transition smoothness that is poorly matched to recommendation, and its codebook gradients can still alter global Voronoi geometry in ways that reduce sequence information or branch diversity. The endpoint barrier protects only sampled transitions and may not prevent level-0 usage concentration or frequency drift. A healthy local residual objective therefore does not guarantee downstream recall or NDCG.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The cosine residual-alignment gradient acts on the selected codewords through both residual subtractions, adjusting the residual coordinate frames rather than directly minimizing endpoint codeword distance. The separate barrier repels selected endpoint codewords only below squared separation s and has zero gradient above it. Thus neither term attracts endpoint codewords; the pair-distance contribution is explicitly repulsive when needed. Assignment indices are stop-gradient.
